locally listed and non-designated heritage coverage
DfT NaPTAN transport-access points and design-stage count gap

accuracy_notes: Archaeological priority area geometries were retained as screening context and not promoted without exact canonical parcel intersection and proposal-specific assessment.
Locally listed and heritage-at-risk records were not treated as legal extent, consent or development outcome without current documents and exact asset or parcel relations.
Local resilience forum boundaries and organisations were retained as administrative routing, not parcel-level hazard, response-time or public-safety scores.
NaPTAN points were not converted into accessibility scores without walking networks, timetables, service frequency and accessible-route evidence.
Built-up-area, green-belt-core and design-code-characteristic records were treated as statistical or category vocabularies rather than parcel policies.
NUAR, aircraft-noise and UK-airport backlog surfaces were retained as coverage gaps; absence of open geometry was never interpreted as absence of assets or constraints.
No parcel relation, future-growth score or business row was fabricated.
